title: Bacterial meningitis (infection of the brain lining)

items: Meningitis is an infection of the membranes that cover the brain and spinal cord.
Bacterial meningitis is an emergency and needs antibiotics straight away.
Fever, a severe headache, and a stiff neck.
Sensitivity to light (photophobia), confusion, and sometimes a rash of small spots that do not fade when pressed.
Lumbar puncture (fluid test around the spine) with cell count, protein, sugar, Gram stain and culture.
Blood cultures, ideally taken before antibiotics if this does not cause delay.
CT scan of the head only if it is needed before the lumbar puncture.
Antibiotics are started straight away, often before the tests are back.
Your team will explain the plan as results come back.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Do not wait at home. Go to hospital straight away if you have these symptoms.
Ask your family to get medical help immediately if you are very unwell.
Your team will check for hearing or memory problems after recovery.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Fever with a stiff neck or a severe headache (emergency: immediate antibiotics are required)
A rash of spots that does not fade when pressed
